why: Each wrong option becomes the worst under a step misread on Exhibit 1: 129 services read as needing 2 mechanics gives A 149 minutes, 172 read as needing 2.5 gives D 140, and 213 read as needing 3 gives C 135, all above B's 126; A and D tie at 112 as the source's tied filler does, and the slips that still pick B (staffing counted on top of the half mechanic, the half left out of the cut options) are named in sourceHas.

B (1, 4, 2, 3, 5) has no slip behind it: it needs quintile 2 (22%) above quintile 3 (30%), and no wrong base, absolute decrease, level ranking or pair of these gives that order; sourceHas lists no ranking filler (A is the ranking by level, C swaps the close quintiles 3 and 4 or follows the absolute decrease).

3,300 uses the sofa range's total cost (57,400 / 17 = 3,376), 2,700 counts only the workshop saving (46,600 / 17 = 2,741), and 2,800 sits in a tight threshold grid about 5% below the answer; picking the nearest option rather than the largest that fits still gives 2,950, as sourceHas names.

Each wrong option becomes the worst under a step misread (180 albums as needing 2 bookbinders gives A 107 minutes, 240 as needing 2.5 gives D 100, 366 as needing 3.5 gives B 92, all above C's 86), or B under reading its 2.5 extra as on top of June's staff; A and D tie at 80 as the source's tied filler does, and the slips that still pick C are named in sourceHas.

A (10% water) reads Office G's bar alone, B (over 20% buildings) and D (over 90% for the three sectors) read Office D's bar alone (25% and 95%), and the simple-average slip that sourceHas names makes no wrong statement true.

0.6% is the answer out by a factor of 10, 1.7% takes grades 1 to 2 only (19% x 9%), and 7.9% includes grade 4 (88% x 9% = 7.92%) and also fits the source's numeric filler, since dividing 68% by 9 gives 7.6%, about 4% away.
B reads the deepest margin as the highest costs, C compares the losses by margin alone, and D applies 2009's margin to 2010's revenue (41 x 2.44 = $100m); each is a fair slip or over-reading.

A is the worst when the original half jeweller is left out of the cut options (163 minutes against B's 144), C when its 2.5 extra are added on top of December's staff (5 jewellers, 253), and D when 54 rings are read as needing 1.5 jewellers (250); all three beat B's 191.

$7.1bn, $9.1bn and $11.1bn are the source's wide evenly spaced grid with its three numeric fillers: 7.1 sits about 7% above the direct-only slip ($6.6bn), 9.1 continues the spacing, and 11.1 sits about 5% below the direct-plus-indirect slip ($11.7bn); leaving a row out of the sum is the slip sourceHas names.

4.1 forgets to divide by the three years, 0.5 is the yearly percent fall in nitrogen sales (0.52) or the phosphate share's total fall (0.49), and 0.2 is the source's numeric filler, continuing the roughly 2.8x spacing below 0.5; counting four years and starting from 2009 are the slips that sourceHas names.
70% uses people instead of visits as the base, 48% takes the complement (repeat visits out of all visits), and 30% makes both slips (repeat visitors out of all people).
A compares the losses by margin alone, B applies 2010's margin to 2011's revenue (36 x 2.61 = EUR 94m), and C reads the deepest margin as the highest costs; each is a fair slip or over-reading.
